summary: First backend test run for HR Copilot AI. Built a pytest suite (69 tests) covering health, signup/login/me/logout, cookie+Bearer auth, bcrypt hash format, CORS, brute-force, team management, full RBAC matrix (org_admin/hr_manager/recruiter/hiring_manager/viewer), multi-tenant isolation (OrgA vs OrgB across jobs/candidates/overview/team), Jobs CRUD + validation, JD generate/save/versioning/refine, resume upload (txt/exe/empty/>10MB) + AI analyze, interview kit generation + scorecard validation, overview dashboard, demo seed/clear idempotency and audit logging. Result: 66 passed / 3 failed (95.6%). Core functionality, RBAC and tenant isolation are solid; 1 functional AI defect (JD Generator returns empty core sections) and 2 security gaps (wildcard CORS with credentials, no brute-force lockout).

critical.issue: Generated JD comes back with EMPTY job_summary, required_skills, preferred_skills, qualifications and experience. RCA: ai_service.generate_job_description appends 'Include only these sections: <include_sections> (fill others with empty string/list)'. The backend default include_sections = ['Company Overview','Responsibilities','KPIs','Benefits','Career Growth','Diversity Statement'] does not name the skills/summary/qualification/experience sections, so Claude deliberately blanks them even though required_skills=['Python','FastAPI','MongoDB'] was supplied. Verified twice: with default sections those 5 fields are empty; passing include_sections including 'Required Skills','Preferred Skills','Qualifications' fills them but then blanks job_summary/career_growth/diversity_statement. The 'include only these' instruction must apply to optional sections only — core fields (job_title, job_summary, responsibilities, required_skills, preferred_skills, qualifications, experience) should always be populated.

allow_credentials=True combined with allow_origins default '*' (CORS_ORIGINS not set). Response returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with Allow-Credentials: true — browsers reject credentialed (httpOnly cookie) requests, so cookie auth cannot work cross-origin, and the wildcard is a security anti-pattern. Set explicit origins from env (e.g. the preview URL) instead of '*'.

minor.issue: No brute-force protection: 6 consecutive wrong-password attempts all return 401, no lockout (expected 423/429 after 5 fails per auth playbook). No rate limiting or failed_attempts counter.

Body typed as raw Dict[str, Any] — no Pydantic validation. Arbitrary/unknown keys (e.g. 'stage' on a job, 'is_demo', 'created_by') are written straight into the document. Confirmed: PATCH /api/jobs with {"stage":"sourcing"} is accepted and persisted although the Job model has no stage field. Recommend a Pydantic update model with a field whitelist.
Salary validation uses `if body.salary_min and body.salary_max` — falsy 0 bypasses the check (salary_min=0 with salary_max=-5 would pass). Use `is not None`.

Gated by require_perm('org.read') then an inline org_admin check. Recruiter/viewer roles lack org.read so they get 403 with detail 'Insufficient permissions: org.read' on a write route — misleading; should be an org.update permission.
When job_id is null, every save creates a brand-new JD document (no version chain possible). Acceptable per spec but the UI cannot version standalone JDs.

action_items: Fix ai_service.generate_job_description prompt: never blank core JD fields (job_summary, required_skills, preferred_skills, qualifications, experience). Restrict the 'include only these sections' instruction to optional sections (Company Overview, KPIs, Benefits, Career Growth, Diversity Statement), or add the core sections to the default include_sections list.
Set explicit CORS origins (from env) instead of '*' since allow_credentials=True; wildcard + credentials breaks cookie auth in browsers.
Add brute-force protection on /api/auth/login (lockout/429 after 5 failed attempts).
Replace raw Dict[str, Any] bodies on PATCH /api/jobs and PATCH /api/candidates with validated Pydantic models + field whitelist.
Use `is not None` for salary_min/salary_max comparisons in create_job and jd_generate.
critical_code_review_comments: ai_service.py L64: 'Include only these sections: ... (fill others with empty string/list)' is the root cause of the empty JD sections — the model treats every schema key not named in include_sections as excluded.
server.py L32-38: CORSMiddleware with allow_credentials=True and allow_origins='*' is invalid for credentialed requests.
routes_hr.py L68 & L242: unvalidated Dict[str, Any] PATCH bodies allow arbitrary field injection into Mongo documents (org_id/id are stripped, but is_demo, created_by, org-level fields are not).
routes_hr.py is 541 lines and mixes jobs/jd/resumes/candidates/interviews/overview/demo; empty /app/backend/routes, /models, /services packages exist — split it up.
deps.py: JWT has no revocation/refresh; logout only clears the cookie so a leaked Bearer token stays valid for 7 days.
routes_hr.py analyze(): weight sum validation happens after the resume/job lookups, so a bad-weights request still costs two DB round-trips — validate on the Pydantic model instead.
seed_data_creation: Created 18 temporary TEST_ orgs/users, TEST_ jobs, candidates, JDs, resumes and interviews via the public API. All removed afterwards with /app/backend/tests/cleanup_test_data.py (18 orgs, 34 users, 14 jobs, 4 JDs, 36 audit logs deleted). Seeded admin org left intact.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Suite lives in /app/backend/tests (conftest.py + 4 test modules) and runs against REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env. Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -v (pytest.ini forces -n 2 --dist loadscope; AI classes take ~55s). Verified PASSING: health, signup/duplicate/short-password, login success+401, /auth/me via Bearer and cookie, httpOnly cookie on login+signup, logout, bcrypt $2b$, team add/list/invalid-role/non-admin-403, full RBAC matrix (recruiter can create jobs; viewer & hiring_manager get 403 on create/update/delete; non-admin demo seed/clear 403), tenant isolation (OrgB sees [] jobs/candidates, 404 on OrgA job/candidate, isolated overview + team), Jobs CRUD + salary 400 + 404s + 422, JD save with version bump to v2 and versions[] ordered [2,1], JD refine, resume upload txt (Emergent Object Storage works, storage_path returned) with 400 on .exe/empty/>10MB, resume analyze (overall_score, matched/missing skills, summary, persisted candidate) plus 404/400 edge cases, interview kit generation (10 questions, plan, competencies, persisted) and scorecard validation (rating 6 -> 400, bad recommendation -> 400, success -> 200), overview shape with all 9 pipeline stages, demo seed (3 jobs/4 candidates is_demo:true), already_loaded idempotency, demo clear removing only is_demo records, audit logs org-scoped. KNOWN FAILING (all real defects, not test issues): test_generate_jd (empty core JD fields), test_cors_allows_credentials (wildcard origin), test_brute_force_lockout (no lockout). Run cleanup_test_data.py after each run. manual_jd_probe.py reproduces the JD-generate defect in ~40s.
rca_of_the_issue: JD Generator empty sections: ai_service.generate_job_description builds the prompt with 'Include only these sections: {include_sections} (fill others with empty string/list)'. JDGenerateIn.include_sections defaults to ['Company Overview','Responsibilities','KPIs','Benefits','Career Growth','Diversity Statement'], which omits the skills/summary/qualifications/experience sections, so Claude Sonnet 5 correctly follows the instruction and returns empty values for those schema keys. Reproduce: POST /api/jd/generate with required_skills=['Python','FastAPI','MongoDB'] and no include_sections -> content.required_skills == [], job_summary == ''. Passing include_sections that explicitly lists 'Required Skills','Preferred Skills','Qualifications' fills them but blanks job_summary/career_growth/diversity_statement, proving causation. Mitigation: apply the exclusion instruction only to optional/marketing sections and always require the core fields to be populated.
